ios.desc:
Your agents keep working. You keep living.

Claude Code runs on your own machine. When it stops to ask, your phone gets the question. Answer with a tap, and it keeps going.

WHILE YOU WERE OUT

2:47 PM. You leave. Claude Code is mid release in ~/dev/acme-api.
3:12 PM. It hits the one thing it cannot decide alone.
3:13 PM. You read the plan in the lunch line and tap Allow.
3:19 PM. Shipped. Your laptop never opened.

WHAT YOU GET

A card for the quick yes. The question arrives as a push and answers like a text.
The real terminal for everything else. Your actual session, live from your machine, for when you want to look around first.
A trackpad. Swipe instead of hunting arrow keys on a phone.
Dictation. Say the next prompt at the speed of thought, not of one thumb.
Every machine you own. macOS, Linux, WSL. Pair them all, one app.

YOUR CODE NEVER MOVES

End to end encrypted, so the relays that carry your traffic cannot read a byte of it. No account, because pairing is a QR code between your phone and your machine. No telemetry. Ciao phones home to your machine and nowhere else.

SETUP IS ONE COMMAND

curl -fsSL https://ciaooo.app/install.sh | sh

It ends at a QR code. Scan it with the app. Then go.

WATCHING IS FREE. ACTING IS PRO.

Pairing, sessions, live output and every notification are free forever. Sending, steering and answering your agents is Ciao Pro, and the first 20 are on the house.

Ciao Pro is $9.99 per month or $89.99 per year, and a new subscription starts with a free week. Payment is charged to your Apple Account when the free week ends. The subscription renews automatically unless it is turned off at least 24 hours before the period ends, and you can manage or cancel it in your Apple Account settings.

quotes.text:
Hi HN,
I built Ciao to solve problems I was experiencing:

1. Connecting to a new host should be as seamless as possible. I SSH a lot nowadays, and I find the key sharing across devices cumbersome.

2. I get annoyed by setting up insert-your-favorite VPN on new machines. They're all great. I don't want to think about them.

3. There's a lot of harnesses: Claude Code and Codex now have decent mobile push notifications but what about Pi or xyz-shiny-new harness? The harness is another tool that should be abstracted out.

4. I want a single application that has the big picture of all of my agents. Tmux and Herdr are great but they don't have an overview of all my connected machines' agents.

---

With Ciao you curl|sh the daemon --> run ciao pair --> point your phone's camera at the QR code --> and you're connected. It uses iroh for accountless and E2EE connection. There's an optional relay server for APNS which too is E2EE.

One of my favorite aspects of agentic-engineering is being able to just have a lot of fun with programming. Among many features, I built a visually pleasing toggle between terminal-mode and native-chat-mode. If you install Ciao, come back here and tell me what you think.

---

Full transparency: this is a repost from yesterday, it was a massive day in AI.
